test.title: The museum that gave things back

paragraphs.text: A city museum in Europe holds four thousand objects collected during the nineteenth century. In 2018 its director announced that the museum would return any item taken without the consent of its owners.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The announcement was easier to make than to carry out. Records from the period are thin, and in many cases nobody can tell whether an object was bought, given or seized. A team of historians now checks each item.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Three collections have gone home so far. Museum attendance has not fallen, and loans from other institutions have increased, which the director takes as a sign that the policy has not damaged the museum.
paragraphs.label: C
